input: Every time I save a TS file I want it run through the same prettier + eslint --fix pipeline — identical result each time, no judgment calls.
expectedOutcome: The whole need is deterministic (prettier + eslint --fix, 'identical result each time, no judgment calls') and the trigger is the USER's own editor save — not the agent's Edit/Write tool event, which is the only thing a Claude hook can fire on. The determinism gate therefore routes this to a script wired to format-on-save / a git pre-commit hook. A Claude hook is the acceptable alternative only if 'save' is read as the agent's own write. NOT a skill/agent — there is no judgment to apply.

input: When I write a PR description, you keep doing it inconsistently — capture the right way to investigate the diff and frame the summary so it's good every time.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a skill (a reusable, judgment-bearing procedure), armed with any deterministic helpers (e.g. a diff-stats script). NOT a pure script — framing needs judgment.

input: For future reference, our staging database is provisioned through Neon and the prod one is on RDS — remember that.
expectedOutcome: Routes to memory (a declarative fact to recall). NOT a rule — it tells the agent what is true, not what to do.

input: Generally, prefer composition over inheritance in this codebase and call it out when reviewing.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a rule (a standing directive applied with judgment, soft-nudge tolerant). NOT memory — it directs behavior, not a fact.

input: Whenever I edit a file in src/generated/, re-run the codegen checksum — it must fire every single time, not just when you remember.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a hook (a guaranteed, mechanical reaction to the agent's own edit). NOT a rule — rules are advisory and can be skipped.

input: Keep an eye on ~/Library/Logs/build.log and ping me when a new ERROR line shows up while I'm working.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a monitor (watch an external file over time). NOT a hook — hooks fire on the agent's own tool events, not on external file changes.

input: I have a Hookdeck endpoint that receives deploy-finished webhooks — when one arrives, I want to be told so I can verify the release.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a monitor (push/inbound-webhook awareness of the world). NOT a hook (own-action only). Degrade gracefully if no push source exists yet.

input: There's a Google Doc sign-up table I check via an expensive MCP tool (huge responses). Watch it and tell me only when a sign-up slot actually changes.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a script (extracts just the slice) chained with a command-poll monitor (diffs it, pages on real delta) — a script+monitor chain. NOT an agent loop re-pulling and diffing in context.

input: I want a capability I can switch on for some subagents and off for others — opt-in, loaded only when relevant.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a skill (per-session/per-subagent toggleable, opt-in). NOT a rule/memory, which apply globally and can't be scoped per subagent.

input: I want a quick shortcut to merge the current PR, but I do NOT want you doing it autonomously — only when I explicitly ask.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a user-invocable (user-only) skill — a shortcut that dissuades autonomous agent use. NOT a rule/hook.

input: I want you to be able to query and mutate our Linear workspace lots of different ways during a session — issues, projects, comments, the whole surface.
expectedOutcome: Routes to mcp (model-driven breadth across many operations, environment permits MCP). A fixed single call would be a script wrapper instead.

input: Our org forbids MCP servers, but I need you to fetch one specific report from an internal API on demand.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a script/CLI wrapper (the fixed capability) plus a skill for semantic activation — the MCP decomposition. NOT a native mcp server.

input: I want to review a 4000-line diff across many files without blowing up your main context — fan it out and bring back just the findings.
expectedOutcome: Routes to an agent (context isolation + parallelism, results summarized back). NOT a skill running inline in the main context.

input: I regularly need to scrape thousands of rows from a CSV and label each with a simple category — it's menial but high-volume.
expectedOutcome: Pushes the mechanical parts to a script, and routes the residual light reasoning to a cheap-tier (e.g. haiku), tool-scoped, disposable subagent. NOT the premium orchestrator doing it inline.

input: I don't want the orchestrating agent ever pulling our giant analytics dataset into its context, but I do need light analysis over it on a recurring basis.
expectedOutcome: Routes to an agent with tool-scoping — forbid the data-retrieval tool in the orchestrator, allow it only in a disposable subagent whose context is throwaway.

input: I have a set of chief-of-staff capabilities — a few skills, a rule, and a hook — that I want to enable for my assistant agent and disable for my coding agent, as one unit.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a plugin (a coherent bundle toggled on/off by context). NOT a single skill — the value is bundling + toggleability.

input: I want to start packaging my customizations as plugins I can turn on and off, but I don't have anywhere to put them yet.
expectedOutcome: Routes to marketplace first (set up a personal marketplace via aipm init), because the plugin primitive requires a marketplace to live in. THEN a plugin.

input: The pdf skill from the anthropic-skills marketplace gets one step wrong for my workflow — fix it so my setup behaves the way I want.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a personal override — a local user-scope skill/rule that shadows the upstream skill — NOT editing the consumer-marketplace skill in place (it's read-only / upstream-owned).

input: Every morning at 6am, rotate yesterday's logs and gzip them. No analysis, no notification — just do it.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a script wired to OS cron — purely mechanical, no agent needed. NOT a monitor (nothing to interpret) and NOT an agent.

input: Any time you edit a file under src/auth/, immediately take a careful second look at that change for security problems and flag anything risky — every edit, without fail.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a hook on the agent's own edit (PostToolUse matching src/auth/) whose reaction is an agentic security review — there is NO deterministic script; the hook just guarantees the agent does the review. NOT a rule (advisory, can be skipped — but this must fire every edit) and NOT a monitor (this is the agent's OWN action, not the world). Tests the hook-without-script path.

input: When I ask you to audit our dependencies, always extract the license of every package the exact same way, then reason about which licenses are legally risky for us to ship.
expectedOutcome: Routes to a skill (semantically activated on 'audit dependencies') armed with a deterministic license-extraction script — the script does the mechanical extraction, the skill carries the risk judgment. NOT a hook (there is no own-action/event trigger) and NOT a bare script (there is real judgment). Tests the script-without-hook path (a deterministic script living inside a skill).
